demand.def: Demand: the quantities of a good buyers are willing and able to buy at each price, shown as a downward-sloping demand curve. The quantity demanded is the amount at one particular price.

law-of-demand.def: The law of demand: other things equal, when a good's price rises the quantity demanded falls, and when it falls the quantity demanded rises.

income-effect.def: Income effect: a lower price makes buyers' income go further, so they can buy more. Substitution effect: a lower price makes the good cheaper than its substitutes, so buyers switch toward it.

market-demand.def: Market demand: the sum of every individual buyer's quantity demanded at each price (a horizontal sum of the individual demand curves).

demand-shifter.def: Determinants of demand: the changes other than the good's own price that shift demand: tastes, income (a normal good's demand rises with income, an inferior good's falls), prices of substitutes and complements, expectations and the number of buyers.
